flagged.text: In another Serbian tale Usud answers the hero's question why a water has no yield: because it has never drowned a person.
flagged.reason: Translation choice: the Serbian text asks why the water has no 'рода' (afanasyev1868:p.234); 'yield' is one reading, but род can also mean offspring or fruit, and the page does not settle which.

grade_rationale.text: Every surviving clause rests on Afanasyev's Poetic Views of the Slavs (volumes 2 and 3, counted as one source), retelling Serbian tales.

Afanasyev says the tale of Fate and the two Dolyas is printed in Karadžić's Serbian tales, and points to a further tale in the Matica edition; neither is a source in this entry, so no second independent author supports a clause.
The verified entry names one people, the Serbs.
One 19th-century compiler and one people give the grade literary: a lone compiler printing collected tales still counts as one source, so the entry cannot reach regional on this corpus.
